verdict.rationale: Both PRs move the email, name and role checks into one module, and both keep the message wording and order intact. B also removes the invite-only case divergence: invitation emails are now lowercased, which `docs/api.md` requires and which closes a duplicate-invite gap. B reports this change and covers it with a test. A keeps that bug alive as a `lowercase: false` option in the shared validator, so the divergence the task wants removed survives, and A adds no tests for the new module.
a_issues: Keeps the documented-contract violation where invitation emails are not lowercased, so duplicate invites can slip past the case-sensitive store check.
Adds a `lowercase` option to `validateEmail` whose only purpose is to keep that bug, which keeps the per-handler divergence the task is meant to remove.
No tests for the new `validation.js` module or for the edge cases it moved, such as the 80/81 character name boundary and rejecting the owner role on invite.
b_issues: Changes observable invite behavior (lowercasing) inside a refactor PR. It is justified by the docs and reported, but it is still a behavior change rather than a pure refactor.
Adds a separate `validateOptionalName` function rather than an option; this is minor, and it reads clearly.
